q: 1. The mass of 2.5 m³ of a certain liquid is 2 tonnes. Its mass density is
explain: Density = Mass / Volume. 2 tonnes = 2000 kg. So, 2000 / 2.5 = 800 kg/m³.

q: 2. The property of a liquid which offers resistance to the movement of one layer of liquid over another adjacent layer of liquid, is called
explain: Viscosity is the internal friction of a fluid that resists the relative motion of its layers.

q: 3. The force per unit length is the unit of
explain: Surface tension is defined as the force acting per unit length (N/m) along the surface of a liquid.

q: 4. The mercury does not wet the glass. This is due to the property of the liquid known as
explain: Mercury has higher cohesive forces (attraction between its own molecules) than adhesive forces (attraction to glass), causing it to avoid 'wetting' the surface.

q: 5. With an increase in size of tube, the rise or depression of liquid in the tube due to surface tension will
options: depend upon the characteristics of liquid
explain: Capillary rise (h) is inversely proportional to the diameter of the tube (d) according to the formula h = (4σ cosθ) / (ρgd).

q: 6. The intensity of pressure at point, in a liquid, is
options: directly proportional to the area of the vessel containing liquid
directly proportional to the depth of liquid from the surface
directly proportional to the length of the vessel containing liquid
inversely proportional to the depth of liquid from the surface
explain: According to hydrostatic law, P = ρgh, meaning pressure increases linearly with depth (h).

q: 7. When the pressure intensity at point is more than the local atmospheric pressure, then the difference of these two pressure is called
explain: Gauge pressure is measured relative to atmospheric pressure. If it is higher, it is specifically called positive gauge pressure.

q: 8. The pressure measured with the help of a piezometer tube is in
explain: A piezometer measures pressure by the vertical height (h) to which the liquid rises in the tube.

q: 9. The point at which the resultant pressure on an immersed surface acts, is known as
explain: The Centre of Pressure is the point where the total hydrostatic force is considered to act.

q: 10. A body floating in a liquid is said to be in neutral equilibrium, if its metacentre
options: coincides with its centre of gravity
lies above its centre of gravity
lies below its centre of gravity
lies between the centre of buoyancy and centre of gravity
explain: In neutral equilibrium, M and G coincide, meaning no restoring or overturning moment is produced when the body is tilted.

q: 11. A flow in which each liquid particle has a definite path, and the paths of individual particles do not cross each other, is called
explain: In streamline (laminar) flow, fluid layers slide over each other without mixing or crossing paths.

q: 12. Barometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressure between two points in a pipe
explain: The barometer is specifically designed to measure local atmospheric pressure.

q: 13. An opening in the side of a tank or vessel such that the liquid surface with the tank is below the top edge of the opening, is called ............
explain: A notch is an opening in the side of a tank such that the liquid level is below the upper edge of the opening. It is primarily used for measuring discharge in small channels.

q: 14. When a cylindrical vessel containing liquid is revolved about its vertical axis at a constant angular velocity, the pressure ............
options: Varies at the square of the radial distance
increases linearly as its radial distance
increases as the square of the radial distance
decreases as the square of the radial distance
explain: In a forced vortex, the pressure head increases with the square of the radius ($P = \frac{\rho \omega^2 r^2}{2}$).

q: 15. The kinematic viscosity of an oil (in stokes) whose specific gravity is 0.95 and viscosity 0.011 poise, is ............
explain:
Kinematic viscosity $
u = \mu/ho = 0.011 / 0.95 \approx 0.0116$ Stokes.

q: 16. A moving fluid mass may be brought to a static equilibrium position, by applying an imaginary inertia force of the same magnitude as that of the accelerating force but in the opposite direction. This statement is called ...............
explain: D-Alembert's principle states that a system can be analyzed as if it were in equilibrium by adding an 'inertial force' to the external forces.

q: 17. An open tank containing liquid is made to move from rest with a uniform acceleration. The angle θ which the free surface of liquid makes with the horizontal is such that ...............
explain: The slope of the free surface in a horizontally accelerated tank is given by the ratio of horizontal acceleration (a) to the acceleration due to gravity (g).

q: 18. The coefficient of viscosity may be determined by ...............
explain: All the listed methods are standard laboratory procedures used to measure the dynamic or kinematic viscosity of various fluids.

q: 19. The force present in a moving liquid is ...............
explain: Fluid dynamics involves several forces including inertia (resistance to change in motion), viscosity (internal friction), and gravity (weight).

q: 20. Viscous force is the ............... of shear stress due to viscosity and cross-sectional area of flow.
explain: Force is defined as Stress × Area. Therefore, viscous force is the product of viscous shear stress and the area over which it acts.

q: 21. A floating body attains stable equilibrium if its metacentre is ...............
explain: Stability is achieved when the Metacentre (M) is above the Centre of Gravity (G). If M is above G, a restoring couple is formed.

q: 22. Centre of buoyancy is ...............
options: centroid of pressure of the displaced liquid
explain: The center of buoyancy is the point through which the upward buoyant force acts, coinciding with the geometric center (centroid) of the displaced liquid volume.

q: 23. The ratio of the maximum height to which a jet inclined through θ rises to its total horizontal span is ...............
explain: Maximum height H = (u² sin²θ)/2g and Range R = (u² sin2θ)/g. The ratio H/R simplifies to 1/4 tan θ.

q: 24. For the flow of liquid from an open ended tube (or nozzle) leading to the formation of spray of liquid drops, the number generally applied, is ...............
explain: Weber number (We) relates inertial force to surface tension, which is the dominant force in drop formation and atomization.

q: 25. Though angle of deviation of liquid is more in internal mouth piece, the contraction of the jet, is
options: more in the internal mouth piece
less in the internal mouth piece
explain: In a Borda’s (internal) mouthpiece running full, the coefficient of contraction is actually higher (less contraction of the final jet) compared to when it's running free.

q: 26. The moment of inertia of a floating body... are I and V respectively. The height of the metacentre above centre of buoyancy of the body, is ...............
explain: The distance between the centre of buoyancy (B) and the metacentre (M) is known as the BM distance, calculated as $BM = I/V$.

q: 27. The radius of gyration of the water line... is 4 m and its metacentric height is 72.5 cm. The period of oscillation of the ship, is ...............
explain: The time period of oscillation is $T = 2\pi \sqrt{k^2 / (g \cdot GM)}$. Using $k=4$, $GM=0.725$, and $g=9.81$, $T$ calculates roughly to $3\pi$.

q: 28. An open container filled with water is moved vertically upward with a uniform linear acceleration. The pressure at its bottom will be ...............
explain: The effective acceleration becomes $(g + a)$. Therefore, the pressure $P = ho(g+a)h$, which is greater than the static pressure $ho gh$.

q: 29. Cavitation is caused by ...............
explain: Cavitation occurs when the local pressure in a liquid drops below its vapor pressure, causing vapor bubbles to form and then collapse violently.

q: 30. An ideal fluid is defined as the fluid which ...............
explain: An ideal fluid is a theoretical fluid that lacks viscosity and cannot be compressed.

q: 31. A Newtonian fluid is defined as the fluid which ...............
explain: A Newtonian fluid is any fluid that maintains a linear relationship between shear stress and velocity gradient (constant viscosity).

q: 32. Fluid statics deals with the following forces ...............
explain: In fluid statics, the fluid is at rest, meaning there are no shear (viscous) forces. Only gravity (body force) and pressure (surface force) are considered.

q: 33. The resultant hydrostatic force acts through a point known as ...............
explain: The centre of pressure is defined as the point on an immersed surface where the total hydrostatic pressure can be considered to act.

q: 34. The point, through which the buoyant force is acting, is called ...............
explain: The centre of buoyancy is the point where the entire upward force of the displaced liquid is considered to act.

q: 35. The point, through which the weight is acting, is called ...............
explain: The centre of gravity ($G$) is the point where the entire weight of the body is concentrated.

q: 36. For a floating body, if the meta-centre is below the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is called
explain: Unstable equilibrium occurs when a small tilt creates an overturning moment, which happens when $M$ is below $G$.

q: 37. For a floating body, if the meta-centre coincides with the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is...
explain: Neutral equilibrium occurs when the body remains in its new position after being tilted, occurring when $M$ and $G$ coincide ($GM = 0$).

q: 38. For a floating body, if centre of buoyancy is above the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is called
explain: If the centre of buoyancy ($B$) is above $G$, the body is inherently stable, as the metacentre ($M$) will necessarily be above $G$.

q: 39. For a submerged body, if the centre of buoyancy is below the centre of gravity, the equilibrium is called
explain: For a submerged body, stability is determined by the relative positions of G (Center of Gravity) and B (Center of Buoyancy). If G is above B, a small displacement creates a couple that increases the tilt, leading to unstable equilibrium.

q: 40. The square root of the ratio of inertia force to gravity force is called
explain: The Froude number represents the square root of (Inertia Force / Gravity Force), commonly used in open channel flow and wave studies.

q: 41. Drag is defined as the force exerted by a flowing fluid on a solid body
options: perpendicular to the direction of flow
in the direction which is at an angle of 45°
explain: Drag is the component of the total force exerted by the fluid on the body in the direction of the relative motion (parallel to the flow).

q: 42. A body is called bluff body if the surface of the body
options: does not coincide with the streamlines
explain: A bluff body has a shape that does not coincide with streamlines, causing flow separation and a large wake, resulting in high pressure drag.
